title: The app shell
summary: Four tabs, a back button that walks back through the app, and a layout that follows the window.
description: The same interface runs on a phone, a tablet and a computer. It is built from a small design system, and its mechanical rules are checked by the build, so a new screen looks like the rest.

requirements.text: The app has four tabs: Exercises, Tutor, Music and Settings.
Exercises is the home screen: today's lessons on top, then the courses.
Android's back button closes a sheet first, then the page, then goes from another tab to Exercises, and leaves the app only from Exercises.
Below 768 px of window width the tabs are at the bottom; from 768 px they form a rail at the left edge.
From 1000 px a course's or a lesson's page is laid out in two columns, and Settings shows its menu beside the open page.
Search lists every word and sentence in the app, met or not, filterable by course and searchable in Polish or English.
On Android the page lays out above the keyboard, and the tab bar is hidden while typing.
Light and dark themes are both supported; the theme is a setting of the device.
Touch targets are at least 44 px, or 36 px in dense rows.
A destructive action asks for confirmation once and says what will be lost.
An empty list says what would be there and offers the action that fills it.
The build fails when a screen breaks the design system's mechanical rules.
